messages.author: 87e100fbbe32313a
messages.subject: Difficulty seeing the dplyr vignette
parts:
Dear Hadley et al. –

 Not sure if this is the proper location to post this – if it should be somewhere else, let me know.

 I can not seem to run the dplyr vignette. All I get is the following message:

Warning message:

vignette ‘introduction’ not found

 I appear to have done a successful installation of devtools and dplyr. I am able to view other vignettes. I have tried running the “vignette("introduction", package = "dplyr")” command both on the R console and on RStudio. (I tried it again on RStudio with the Sweave option set to knitr. I have run it cut-and-pasted from the dplyr page (to avoid accidental misspellings) and typed out (to avoid possible invisible characters). The vignette() command appears to find most of the vignettes for packages I have installed.  I have installed and uninstalled the dplyr package several times.

I have read, here: http://www.bioconductor.org/help/package-vignettes/   that vignette files are usually in the program’s doc directory. The version of dplyr that I have installed does not contain a doc directory. I could not find any .Rnw files either.

 I do have plyr installed, but not loaded.

 Any suggestions for finding or fixing this problem greatly appreciated.  I am running under MS-Windows XP SP3; My sessionInfo() results are below.

 Sincerely, Andrew

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Difficulty seeing the dplyr vignette
parts:
Hmmm, I hadn't thought about this. To build the vignette yourself,
you'll need to install all the suggested packages as well. Vignette
building is currently probably one of the big advantages of CRAN, and
I'm not sure how to simulate locally, because you need not only the
required (and imported packages), but potentially all of the suggested
packages as well. The metadata in DESCRIPTION is not quite fine
grained enough to be able to do this efficiently - I don't really want
to default to installing all suggested packages.

One solution would be to distribute the builds made by Travis in the
course of testing, but I don't have a workflow for this yet.

Hadley
